anvil:aws:VpcEndpoint.description: An Anvil-managed AWS Interface VPC Endpoint. Creates one ENI per private subnet with private DNS enabled. The endpoint security group starts with zero rules. Passing this endpoint to a grant (e.g. queue.grantSendMessage(fn, { endpoint: sqsEndpoint })) adds a one-way ingress rule on port 443 from that compute's own security group, so only granted compute can reach the endpoint. Access is enforced at three layers: network (one-way SG rules per grant), IAM role policy (scoped per grant and limited to this endpoint with aws:SourceVpce), and endpoint policy (ceiling on allowed actions for principals in this account).

vpcId.description: The ID of the VPC to create the endpoint in. Accepts both Anvil-managed VPC IDs and imported VPC IDs.

privateSubnetIds.description: The IDs of the private subnets to attach the endpoint to. AWS places one ENI per subnet. Pass all private subnet IDs from your VPC — typically one per AZ.

service.description: The AWS service to route privately. The full com.amazonaws.{region}.{service} name is constructed at deploy time from the resolved region — you never write it manually.

overridePermissions.description: Explicit Allow and Deny permission statements for the endpoint policy. When omitted, the endpoint policy allows all actions (*) for principals in this account. When set, only the declared actions are permitted — the caller is responsible for declaring every action their compute resources need. Supports both Allow and Deny effects. Every statement is limited to principals in this account. Resource defaults to "*" if omitted on a permission entry.

allowAllOutbound.description: Adds, on the endpoint's security group, the rule AWS puts on a new security group (all traffic to 0.0.0.0/0). Off by default, and an endpoint only replies so it never needs it: Anvil security groups start with no outbound rules. Logs a preview warning when on. App.defaults.vpc.allowAllOutbound sets it for every Anvil security group in the app; an explicit value here wins.

endpointId.description: The ID of the VPC endpoint, e.g. vpce-0abc1234567890abc. Use this to reference the endpoint in IAM condition keys such as aws:SourceVpce.

dnsName.description: The first DNS name assigned to the endpoint, e.g. vpce-xxx.sqs.ap-southeast-2.vpce.amazonaws.com. With private DNS enabled, normal consumers use the standard AWS SDK hostname — this is exposed for debugging and multi-VPC architectures only.

securityGroupId.description: The ID of the dedicated security group attached to this endpoint. It starts with zero rules; each grant that passes this endpoint adds ingress on port 443 from the granted compute's own security group.

service.description: The AWS service this endpoint routes, e.g. "sqs". Grants check it against the service being granted.

anvil:aws:VpcEndpointPermission.description: A single permission statement in the VPC endpoint policy. Effect must be Allow or Deny. Action is an IAM action string. Resource defaults to * if omitted.

resource.description: The ARN to scope this permission to. Defaults to "*" if omitted — applies to all resources of this service. Accepts Output<string> — pass resource ARNs directly, e.g. queue.arn, secret.arn.
